@updates.failure.check.description: Shown in the menu-triggered update-check toast and in the status line of Settings > Updates & privacy when a check for a new version didn't get an answer. {reason} is one or two complete, already-translated sentences saying why and what to do (for example "Cmdr couldn't reach its server. Check your internet connection and try again."), so end your sentence with a period and let the reason follow it. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate). Avoid the words "error" and "failed".

placeholders.reason: one or two already-translated sentences saying why the check didn't get an answer and what to do; Cmdr controls the wording but the length varies

@updates.failure.check.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.checkUntyped: Cmdr couldn’t check for updates. Check your internet connection and try again later.

@updates.failure.checkUntyped.description: Same place as updates.failure.check, used when Cmdr can't tell why the check didn't get an answer (usually the internet connection). Two sentences: what didn't happen, then what to try. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate). Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.checkUntyped.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.download: Cmdr couldn’t download the update. Try again later.

@updates.failure.download.description: Shown in the update-check toast and in Settings > Updates & privacy when a new version was found but downloading it didn't finish. Nothing was installed, and the current version keeps working. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate). Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.download.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.install: Cmdr couldn’t install the update. Try again later, or get the latest Cmdr from getcmdr.com.

@updates.failure.install.description: Shown in the update-check toast and in Settings > Updates & privacy when a new version was downloaded but writing it into the app didn't finish. Points at the website as the fallback. "Cmdr" is the product name and "getcmdr.com" the website address: keep both exactly as-is. Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.install.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.failure.notGenuine: Cmdr didn’t install this update: it isn’t a genuine Cmdr release.

@updates.failure.notGenuine.description: Shown in the update-check toast and in Settings > Updates & privacy when an offered update didn't carry Cmdr's signature, so Cmdr refused it and installed nothing. Serious: it may mean someone is tampering with updates. Must read the same as the title of the security notice for this (securityNotices.updateNotGenuine.title). "Cmdr" is the product name. Avoid the words "error" and "failed".
@updates.failure.notGenuine.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.toast.ready: A new version of Cmdr is ready.

@updates.toast.ready.description: Headline of the persistent toast that appears once an update has been downloaded and written into the app. It states the situation; the line below it says what happens next. Sentence case.
@updates.toast.ready.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.toast.readyDetail: Restart now, or you’ll get it the next time you open Cmdr.

@updates.toast.readyDetail.description: Second line of the update-ready toast, under the headline. Reassures the user that doing nothing still gets them the new version: the update is already written to disk and only needs a fresh launch to take effect. Conversational, and the point it has to land is that no action is required.
@updates.toast.readyDetail.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.toast.securityFix: This update fixes {count, plural, one {a security issue} other {# security issues}}.

@updates.toast.securityFix.description: Headline of the persistent update-ready toast when the downloaded update fixes one or more security vulnerabilities. Replaces updates.toast.ready for such updates. States the situation calmly, without alarm: the fix is already downloaded and written into the app. {count} is how many vulnerabilities it fixes; the singular form says "a security issue" rather than a numeral. Sentence case.

placeholders.count: how many security issues the update fixes, 1 or more

@updates.toast.securityFix.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.toast.securityFixDetail: Restart Cmdr to finish installing it.

@updates.toast.securityFixDetail.description: Second line of the security variant of the update-ready toast, under updates.toast.securityFix. Says what to do: restarting is the one step left before the security fix takes effect ("it" is the update). Paired with "Restart now" and "Later" buttons; nothing forces the restart. "Cmdr" is the product name (do not translate).
@updates.toast.securityFixDetail.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.readAdvisory.description: Link in the security variant of the update-ready toast that opens the public security advisory (on GitHub or the Cmdr website) describing what the update fixes and what to do. A short link label, not a sentence.
@updates.toast.readAdvisory.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.versionChange.description: Small, dimmed metadata line at the bottom of the update-ready toast, showing which version replaces which. Version numbers and an arrow only, with no words to translate; the literal "v" prefix and the arrow are both intentional. Keep it identical to English unless your language writes version numbers differently.

placeholders.prev: the version the user is running right now (for example 0.28.3)
placeholders.next: the version that has been downloaded and will run after a restart (for example 0.29.0)

@updates.toast.versionChange.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.versionChangeAria.description: Accessible name for the version line above, which a screen reader would otherwise read out as a bare arrow symbol. Never visible on screen. A plain sentence naming both versions.

placeholders.prev: the version the user is running right now (for example 0.28.3)
placeholders.next: the version that has been downloaded and will run after a restart (for example 0.29.0)

@updates.toast.versionChangeAria.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.later.description: Button that dismisses the update-available toast without restarting now. Tight mini button.
@updates.toast.later.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.toast.restart.description: Button that restarts the app immediately so the already-downloaded update takes effect. Paired with a "Later" button that dismisses the toast. Tight mini button, so keep it short.
@updates.toast.restart.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.unwritable.adminHeadline: Cmdr {version} is ready, but Cmdr can’t install it itself

@updates.unwritable.adminHeadline.description: Bold first line of a warning toast that stays until dismissed. A newer Cmdr is out, but this Mac's copy of the app belongs to another account (typically installed by an administrator or a company's IT tools), so Cmdr can't update itself. Shown to people who ARE administrators of this Mac, so they can fix it themselves. Not an error: a calm statement. "Cmdr" is the product name, never translated.

placeholders.version: the newer version that is out (for example 0.54.0)

@updates.unwritable.adminHeadline.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.unwritable.adminDetail: {path} belongs to another account. To update, download Cmdr from <website>getcmdr.com</website> and drag it into Applications. macOS will ask for your password.

@updates.unwritable.adminDetail.description: Second line of the same warning toast (see updates.unwritable.adminHeadline), telling an administrator how to update by hand: download the app again from the website and drag it into the Applications folder, replacing the old copy. macOS then asks for their password, which is expected. <website> wraps a link that opens the website; keep "getcmdr.com" exactly as is. "Applications" is the macOS folder name: use the name macOS shows for that folder in the target language.

placeholders.path: the full path of the app on disk (for example /Applications/Cmdr.app), never translated

@updates.unwritable.adminDetail.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.unwritable.standardHeadline.description: Bold first line of a warning toast that stays until dismissed. A newer Cmdr is out, but the person's account can't update the app on this Mac (typically a work Mac where the company's IT team installs software, and the person isn't an administrator). "Cmdr" is the product name, never translated.

placeholders.version: the newer version that is out (for example 0.54.0)

@updates.unwritable.standardHeadline.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.unwritable.standardDetail: Your account can’t update Cmdr on this Mac. Ask your IT team, or whoever manages this Mac, to update it.

@updates.unwritable.standardDetail.description: Second line of the same warning toast (see updates.unwritable.standardHeadline). Tells someone without administrator rights who can update the app for them: their company's IT team on a work Mac, or whoever set up and manages the Mac at home. Friendly and practical, not an error.
@updates.unwritable.standardDetail.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title: Move Cmdr to your Applications folder

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.title.description: Title of the dialog shown when a new version is available but Cmdr is running from somewhere it can't update itself. Sentence case. "Applications" is the macOS folder name, which Apple localizes per system language.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.translo: A new version is ready, but macOS is running Cmdr from a temporary read-only copy of itself. That’s what happens when you open an app straight from where you downloaded it, and it means updates have nowhere to land.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.transl.description: First paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog, for the macOS App Translocation case (the app was opened from the Downloads folder). Explains why the update can't be applied. Conversational.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOnl: A new version is ready, but Cmdr is running from a read-only spot, usually a disk image that’s still mounted. That means updates have nowhere to land.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.readOn.description: First paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog, for the case where the app runs from a read-only volume such as a mounted .dmg disk image. Conversational.

updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo: Quit Cmdr, drag it into your Applications folder, and open it from there. Every update after that arrives on its own.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.howTo.description: Second paragraph of the move-to-Applications dialog: the instruction the user should follow. "Applications" is the macOS folder name, which Apple localizes per system language.

@updates.moveToApplicationsDialog.gotIt.description: The only button in the move-to-Applications dialog; closes it. Short, friendly acknowledgement.

updates.status.noUpdates: No updates found. Current version: v{version}

@updates.status.noUpdates.description: Status line after a successful update check that found nothing newer, reporting the current version. The v prefix before the version number is literal.

placeholders.version: the current app version number (for example 0.23.1)

@updates.status.noUpdates.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.status.checking.description: Status line shown while an update check is in progress. Ends with a single ellipsis character.
@updates.status.checking.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.status.downloading.description: Status line shown while a found update is downloading, naming the new and current versions. The v prefixes are literal; ends with a single ellipsis character.

placeholders.next: the new version being downloaded (for example 0.24.0)

@updates.status.downloading.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

@updates.status.installing.description: Status line shown while a downloaded update is installing, naming the new and current versions. The v prefixes are literal; ends with a single ellipsis character.

placeholders.next: the new version being installed (for example 0.24.0)

@updates.status.installing.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.status.managedOff: Your organization manages updates for Cmdr.

@updates.status.managedOff.description: Status line after an update check, when the person's organization (their employer's IT team, through a device-management profile) has turned off updates for Cmdr, so no check ran. Shown in Settings and in the toast after the person picks "Check for updates" from the menu. Not an error: a calm statement of who decides.
@updates.status.managedOff.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.status.heldByPolicy: Cmdr {available} is out, but your organization keeps this Mac on {ceiling} or earlier.

@updates.status.heldByPolicy.description: Status line after an update check that found a newer release which the person's organization (their employer's IT team, through a device-management profile) doesn't allow yet, because it limits Cmdr to a maximum version. Not an error. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

placeholders.available: the newer version that is out (for example 0.53.0)
placeholders.ceiling: the highest version the organization allows, as the IT team wrote it (for example 0.52 or 0.52.3)

@updates.status.heldByPolicy.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.status.unwritableAdmin: Cmdr {version} is out, but Cmdr can’t install it itself. Download it from getcmdr.com and drag it into Applications.

@updates.status.unwritableAdmin.description: Status line in Settings > Updates & privacy (and the toast after the person picks "Check for updates"), when a newer Cmdr is out but this Mac's copy of the app belongs to another account, so Cmdr can't update itself. Shown to administrators, who can replace the app by hand: download it again from the website and drag it into the Applications folder. Keep "getcmdr.com" exactly as is. "Applications" is the macOS folder name: use the name macOS shows for that folder in the target language. Not an error.

placeholders.version: the newer version that is out (for example 0.54.0)

@updates.status.unwritableAdmin.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.status.unwritableStandard: Cmdr {version} is out, but your account can’t update Cmdr on this Mac.

@updates.status.unwritableStandard.description: Status line in Settings > Updates & privacy (and the toast after the person picks "Check for updates"), when a newer Cmdr is out but the person's account can't update the app on this Mac, typically a work Mac whose IT team installs software. Not an error: a calm statement.

placeholders.version: the newer version that is out (for example 0.54.0)

@updates.status.unwritableStandard.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.

updates.status.ready: Update v{next} ready. Restart to apply.

@updates.status.ready.description: Status line shown when an update is downloaded and ready, prompting a restart. The v prefix is literal.
@updates.status.ready.screenshotNote: App-update messaging. The status line renders in the Settings > Updates & privacy panel pictured here, and the update toasts appear while that check runs. Version numbers are substituted, not translated.
